TaskDescription: Participants listened to 20 synthesized sentences while reading them on screen, imagined repeating each sentence without overt movement, and then performed paced imagined syllabification supported by phonetic syllable cues.
Instructions: You will repeat 20 sentences. Each sentence will appear on the screen while it is played by a speech synthesizer. When playback ends, you will have three seconds to finish reading and prepare to repeat it. When the sentence disappears from the screen, you will have five seconds to imagine repeating it. You will then imagine repeating it again, this time syllabifying at the prescribed pace. The syllables will appear on the screen to assist you. Pay attention: the notation is phonetic, so some syllables may look different from what you expect. Imagine that you have something to say, but you cannot say it out loud or show any facial expression. You should feel your jaw, lips, tongue, and vocal cords as if they were about to activate, but in reality, you remain motionless.
